headline: Namma Yatri raises ₹27.25 crore from Dell Foundation

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body: Namma Yatri, the open-source ride-hailing platform backed by payment infrastructure company Juspay, raised ₹27.25 crore (~$3.2M) from Dell Foundation in a pre-Series A round. The company operates a zero-commission model for drivers, charging only a small subscription fee. It reported FY26 revenue of ₹37.5 crore and a net loss of ₹43.8 crore. Namma Yatri is built on the open-source Beckn protocol and operates across several Indian cities including Bengaluru, Delhi and Hyderabad.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: Namma Yatri is the highest-profile test of whether a zero-commission, open-source marketplace can compete with VC-backed incumbents like Uber and Ola. The Dell Foundation investment (philanthropic, not venture capital) signals that impact investors see the model as viable, but the numbers tell a different story: the company is losing more than its entire revenue. The question is whether the zero-commission model can achieve enough driver supply density to compete on reliability — the metric that actually determines rider retention.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Track Namma Yatri's driver count and ride completion rates in Bengaluru, its strongest market. If the zero-commission model can reach supply density parity with Uber in one city, it proves the model; if not, the losses will mount. Watch whether Juspay's backing translates to payment infrastructure advantages and whether other cities adopt the Beckn protocol for mobility.
